method: Full four source/test files read, SHA256/Git blobs verified against pinned tree. Static review, no external requests or Jest execution.
findings: Pagination returns resolved page objects, so library.ts direct reduction is consistent. Deduplicator redundant Promise.all on resolved page objects is harmless under that contract; prior potential mismatch resolved.

Pagination allocates ceil((total-limit-offset)/limit) slots without input validation. For a short final page (e.g.total1,limit25,offset0), ceil negative fraction gives0 and initial page still included. Negative whole counts/zero limit could throw; no malformed-metadata control executed.

Progress callback increments before awaiting current page, so100percent can precede last page success. onError=true can skip failed pages but returns ordinary pages without completeness marker; actual caller policies need review.
Pagination strips all original query parameters then rebuilds offset/limit, risking loss of filters. Fixed initial total/offset pagination has no snapshot/dedup guard against changing playlist.

API playlist deletion sends positions only, without snapshot_id despite type exposing it. Descending batches mitigate index shifts from own deletions but do not establish concurrent-edit safety. Current Spotify API acceptance not checked.

parseAPIResponse checks response.ok after customFetch refreshed retry, so unchecked raw refreshed response is subsequently rejected for these wrapper calls. Earlier customFetch finding is narrowed to direct callers/absence of retries, not unconditional false success.

Existing removal test uses immediately fulfilled saved-track API mocks and asserts call count only; it cannot detect pending completion issue reproduced in v1. Starred test asserts rejection but not zero API calls. No delayed-failure/cancellation snapshot checks seen here.
limits: No upstream Jest/app runtime, external API changes, UI/media or fullplatform proof. pHash/ASAN remains deferred.
